newsitem.title: CHINA: Dalian soybeans end higher on drought reports.
newsitem.headline: Dalian soybeans end higher on drought reports.

text.p: Soybean futures traded at the Dalian Commodity Exchange ended mostly higher on Monday on short-covering triggered by reports of drought in key growing areas, traders said.
But volume shrank, suggesting that the market was not yet convinced of the severity of the dry weather affecting northern China, they said.
The key November 1997 contract ended at an intraday high of 2,844 yuan ($343) per tonne, rising five yuan. It opened at 2,838 and hit a low of 2,830.
"Trading was not active today as investors were unsure about market fundamentals following the official media reports of drought in Shandong and Inner Mongolia," a trader said.
"But the lack of selling also stabilised sentiment today after falls over the past few trading days," he said.
September rose four yuan to 3,102, the January 1998 contract was unchanged at 2,758, and March added seven to 2,764. May fell two to 2,836 and July lost 12 to 2,900.
Combined volume fell to 698,700 tonnes from 1,312,940.
"Investors are sidelined, waiting for a clearer outlook," another trader said.
Traders said they expected soybeans to consolidate at low levels over the next few days, with the market waiting for fresh market-moving news.
